newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks shrug off Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks shrug off Wall Street gains.

text.p: Singapore stocks, weighed down by poor local sentiment, fell early on Friday after briefly attempting higher levels on Wall Street's gains, dealers said.

"The focus in on Singapore and Asia. Wall Street is not ruling the market now," said a dealer. He said factors under close scrutiny included corporate results, especially of index-linked soft drink company Fraser & Neave's.

"Bad results from F&N could just be the last straw which breaks the camel's back," the dealer said, referring to the possibility of F&N pushing the Straits Times Industrials (STI) index below key technical support of 1,982.00.
The results were due after the market closes at 0900 GMT.
At 0200 GMT, the ndex eased from 1,995.82 to 1,986.50, down 4.18 points. Total turnover was a paltry 17 million shares, with 87 gainers and 31 losers.

HongKong Land was active with over 1.8 million shares, underpinned after another member of the Jardine group, Jardine Matheson, said its businesses had performed within expectations. The shares were up US$0.06 at US$2.62.
Property firm Wing Tai, fresh from submitting agressive bids in a Singapore land tender, lost S$0.08 to S$4.22 after it sought to raise up to US$200 million.
